messages:
emma: Quick note from onboarding smoke: if the sample recreates http.Client on token refresh, long Generator streams die mid-run and users see a bland EOF/cancel.
raj: Yup. We hit "rpc error: code = Canceled desc = stream terminated by peer" in QA and it looked like "finished".
stef: That's the classic transport-churn footgun. For samples we should prefer a token-hot-swap RoundTripper that reads token from an atomic store instead of replacing the client.
emma: Can you paste the tiny pattern? I'll update the repo.
stef: Snippet:
```go
var token atomic.Value // stores string
rt := &AuthRT{Base: http.DefaultTransport, TokenFunc: func() string { return token.Load().(string) }}
client := &http.Client{Transport: rt}
// update token.Store(newToken) on refresh
```
No client recreation, preserves TCP/TLS and keeps stream alive.
raj: SDK ergonomics request: iterator.Next currently can block and return confusing Err strings when ctx cancels or auth rotates. Can we add NextContext(ctx) and a Close() on iterator plus typed errors?
emma: Yes. We need ErrCanceledByContext, ErrAuthRotated, ErrConnReset exported so apps don't parse raw grpc/io strings.
stef: Also propose a small helper: StreamReconnect(ctx, req, opts) that will optionally retry once on ErrAuthRotated (configurable), with sensible backoff and honoring ctx. Docs show both patterns: prefer token hot-swap; fallback: explicit reconnect helper.
raj: For implementation: runtime could send a gRPC status with code PermissionDenied + header X-RW-Auth-Rotated mid-stream. SDK maps that to ErrAuthRotated. For transport resets map to ErrConnReset.
emma: Good. We also saw goroutine leaks when handler deadline fires and Next() is blocked. NextContext would help, but Close must cancel internal pumps immediately.
stef: Agreed. API sketch:
```go
// usage in handler
iter := client.Generator.Stream(req.Context(), req)
defer iter.Close()
for iter.NextContext(ctx) { // ctx is handler ctx or per-iteration timeout
  chunk := iter.Token()
}
if errors.Is(iter.Err(), sdk.ErrCanceledByContext) { /* show timeout */ }
```
This keeps callsites simple and explicit.
raj: I'll wire tiny CI test that simulates mid-stream auth rotation and asserts: a) RoundTripper sample keeps stream alive, b) helper retries on ErrAuthRotated when opts.RetryOnAuthRotate=true, c) NextContext returns promptly on ctx cancel and Err() == ErrCanceledByContext.
emma: I'll open docs PR updating onboarding with: 1) token-hot-swap sample, 2) explicit recreate-with-reconnect example, 3) troubleshooting FAQ for "rpc error: code = Canceled" with checklist.
devex-bot: created DEVEX-3245: go-sdk generator ergonomics: NextContext/Close/typed errors + StreamReconnect helper + onboarding samples (link) :white_check_mark:
stef: One more small DX win: expose helper functions IsRetryableStreamError(err) and IsAuthRotateError(err) so app code can branch without importing sdk internals.
emma: Love it. That'll reduce help-desk hits. I'll attach pprof and handshake logs to the ticket after I reproduce locally.
raj: I'll draft the error types and the helper API. Happy to pair on the CI harness.
emma: Thanks all 44d
